zh.principle: **协议**：DTLS 连接 ID（DTLS Connection ID）。RFC 9146 的作用写在其 §1：「This document defines an extension to DTLS 1.2 to add a Connection ID (CID) to the DTLS record layer.」协商通过 §3 定义的扩展完成，「enum { connection_id(54), (65535) } ExtensionType;」；记录层用新的内容类型区分：§4「connections that have negotiated this extension use a distinguished record type tls12_cid(25).」真实内容类型被移到密文内部。
zh.why: 根因是记录层靠五元组挑选安全关联：摘要说「selecting a security association of an incoming DTLS record is accomplished with the help of the 5-tuple」，而§1 说「In DTLS as specified in RFC 6347, the IP address and port of the peer are used to identify the DTLS association.」并指出「Unfortunately, in some cases, such as NAT rebinding, these values are insufficient.」以及受影响最大的场景：「This is a particular issue in the Internet of Things when devices enter extended sleep periods to increase their battery lifetime.」顺带按 TLS 1.3 的实践收紧元数据——记录类型被加密，并提供了填充。
zh.used: 方向语义由零长度值表达：§3「A zero-length CID value indicates that the client is prepared to send using a CID but does not wish the server to use one when sending.」明文记录不受影响（§4「Plaintext records are not impacted by this extension.」）。地址更新被严格设条件：§6 收到源地址不同的记录时「the receiver MUST NOT replace the address it uses for sending records to its peer with the source address specified in the received datagram」除非该报文通过密码学校验、比已知最新报文更新、且有手段确认新地址可达。
zh.broken: 三个限制。其一没有中途换号能力：§3「There is no dedicated “CID update” message that allows new CIDs to be established mid-session」。其二隐私代价明写在 §8：「The CID replaces the previously used 5-tuple and, as such, introduces an identifier that remains persistent during the lifetime of a DTLS connection.」并据此建议多宿主与移动场景改用 DTLS 1.3——「The lack of a CID update mechanism in DTLS 1.2 makes this extension unsuitable for mobility scenarios where correlation must be considered.」其三 §9 承认反射攻击面：对端无法分辨真实地址更新与伪造更新。
zh.history: RFC 9146 由 E.Rescorla（Ed.，Mozilla）、H.Tschofenig（Ed.，Arm Limited）、T.Fossati 与 A.

en.principle: **Protocol**: DTLS Connection ID (DTLS 连接 ID). RFC 9146 states the job in §1: "This document defines an extension to DTLS 1.2 to add a Connection ID (CID) to the DTLS record layer." Negotiation uses the extension defined in §3, "enum { connection_id(54), (65535) } ExtensionType;", and §4 marks the records: "connections that have negotiated this extension use a distinguished record type tls12_cid(25)." with the real content type moved inside the ciphertext.
en.why: The reason is that records pick associations by 5-tuple: the abstract says "selecting a security association of an incoming DTLS record is accomplished with the help of the 5-tuple", and §1 says "In DTLS as specified in RFC 6347, the IP address and port of the peer are used to identify the DTLS association." and "Unfortunately, in some cases, such as NAT rebinding, these values are insufficient." naming the worst-affected setting — "This is a particular issue in the Internet of Things when devices enter extended sleep periods to increase their battery lifetime." Following TLS 1.3 practice, the record type is encrypted and padding is provided.
en.used: Direction is expressed with zero length: §3 states "A zero-length CID value indicates that the client is prepared to send using a CID but does not wish the server to use one when sending." and plaintext records are untouched — §4 "Plaintext records are not impacted by this extension." Address updates are gated: on receiving a record from a different source address §6 says "the receiver MUST NOT replace the address it uses for sending records to its peer with the source address specified in the received datagram" unless the datagram verified cryptographically, is newer than the latest known, and there is a way to confirm the new address is reachable.
en.broken: Three limits. There is no mid-session rotation — §3: "There is no dedicated “CID update” message that allows new CIDs to be established mid-session". §8 states the privacy cost: "The CID replaces the previously used 5-tuple and, as such, introduces an identifier that remains persistent during the lifetime of a DTLS connection." and recommends DTLS 1.3 for multihoming — "The lack of a CID update mechanism in DTLS 1.2 makes this extension unsuitable for mobility scenarios where correlation must be considered." §9 admits the reflection surface: a peer cannot tell a genuine address update from a malicious one.
en.history: RFC 9146 is signed by E. Rescorla (Ed., Mozilla), H. Tschofenig (Ed., Arm Limited), T. Fossati and A. Kraus (Bosch.IO GmbH), published March 2022 as a Standards Track document with “Updates: 6347” in the header. §4 notes the division of labour with its successor: "[DTLS13] specifies how to carry the CID in DTLS 1.3." — this document covers only the DTLS 1.2 record-layer change.

zh: CID：替代五元组的连接标识。
connection_id(54)：协商该扩展的 TLS 扩展号。
tls12_cid(25)：带 CID 的记录内容类型。
NAT 重绑定：端点地址在会话中途改变。
DTLSInnerPlaintext：把真实类型与填充封进密文的结构。
可达性校验：换址前确认新地址能收包。
en: CID: a connection identifier replacing the five-tuple.
connection_id(54): the extension type used to negotiate it.
tls12_cid(25): the record content type that carries a CID.
NAT rebinding: the peer address changes mid-session.
DTLSInnerPlaintext: real type and padding sealed inside the ciphertext.
Reachability check: confirming the new address can receive before switching.
